questions.questionText: The work done in moving a charge of 2 C across two points having a potential difference of 12 V is:
questions.solution: Work = qV = 2 x 12 = 24 J.

questions.questionText: The electric potential at a point on the equatorial line of an electric dipole is:
questions.solution: On the equatorial plane contributions from +q and -q cancel giving zero potential.

questions.questionText: Equipotential surfaces due to a single point charge are:
questions.solution: Radial symmetry means equipotential surfaces are concentric spheres.

questions.questionText: The capacitance of a parallel plate capacitor increases with:
questions.solution: C = kE0A/d. Dielectric with k>1 increases capacitance.

questions.questionText: Two capacitors of 2 uF and 3 uF in series have equivalent capacitance:
Energy stored in a capacitor charged to voltage V is:
The SI unit of electric potential is:
questions.solution: Electric potential is measured in volts (V = J/C).

questions.questionText: A dielectric of constant K inserted in a charged isolated capacitor changes stored energy by:
questions.solution: Q constant, U = Q^2/2C. C increases by K so U decreases by K.

questions.questionText: The electric field is always perpendicular to:
questions.solution: No work along equipotential means E is perpendicular to it.

questions.questionText: A capacitor charged to 200 V stores 1 J. Its capacitance is:
The potential at infinity is conventionally taken as:
questions.solution: By convention potential at infinity is zero.

questions.questionText: In a region of constant potential the electric field is:
questions.solution: E = -dV/dr = 0 when V is constant.

questions.questionText: Three capacitors each of 6 uF in parallel give net capacitance:
questions.solution: Parallel: C = 6+6+6 = 18 uF.

questions.questionText: The relation between electric field E and potential V is:
questions.solution: E = -dV/dr (negative gradient of potential).

questions.questionText: A Van de Graaff generator is used to:
questions.solution: It accumulates charge on a sphere to produce very high potentials.

questions.questionText: Capacitance of a spherical conductor of radius R is:
questions.solution: For an isolated sphere C = 4 pi e0 R.

questions.questionText: Two identical capacitors C in series give equivalent capacitance:
questions.solution: Series: 1/Ceq = 1/C + 1/C = 2/C so Ceq = C/2.

questions.questionText: PE of two charges q1 and q2 separated by r is:
questions.solution: Electrostatic PE U = kq1q2/r.

questions.questionText: Doubling the plate separation of an air capacitor changes C to:
questions.solution: C = e0 A/d. Doubling d halves C.

questions.questionText: An electron moves from 10 V to 0 V. Work done by electric field is:
Dielectric strength is the maximum:
questions.solution: Dielectric strength is the max E field before breakdown.

questions.questionText: If V = 3x + 4y - 5z volts the electric field magnitude is:
questions.solution: E = sqrt(9+16+25) = sqrt(50) = 5 sqrt(2) V/m.

questions.questionText: Capacitance does NOT depend on:
questions.solution: C depends on geometry and dielectric not on charge.

questions.questionText: Potential at midpoint of +q and -q separated by d is:
questions.solution: Equal and opposite contributions cancel: V = 0.
